newsitem.title: USA: Cracker Barrel year-end profits down.
newsitem.headline: Cracker Barrel year-end profits down.

text.p: LEBANON, Tenn., Sept 11 (Reuter) Cracker Barrel Old Country Store, Inc. said Wednesday its profits fell for the fiscal year, citing charges totalling $23 million.
The Lebanon, Tenn.-based restaurant operator said its net income for the year ending Aug.2 fell to $6.7 million from $8.4 million last year.
It said it took a $14.2 million one-time pre-tax charge and an $8.8 million after-tax charge to cover store closings and other items.

The previously announced pre-tax charge covered the closing of three stores; costs of replacing a point-of-sale system; and costs associated with closing its three Cracker Barrel Old Country Store Corner Markets.

Net sales for the fourth quarter were up 28 percent to $282.2 million compared with $221.2 million in the fourth quarter of last year. Sales for the year rose 20 percent to $943 million from $783 million.
Dan W. Evins, chairman and chief executive officer, said the company can achieve growth with its plans to open 50 new stores in 1997.
Cracker Barrel's stock rose 62.5 cents to $23.375 in midday trading on Nasdaq.
